content.title: About
content.content: Johnnycake is a traditional American flatbread made from cornmeal, water and salt. The batter is cooked on a skillet or baked until a golden crust forms. Johnnycake has a dense, slightly crumbly texture and a distinctive corn flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Johnnycake originated in New England in the 17th century as a simple way to use cornmeal brought by European settlers.
The name "johnnycake" is thought to derive from "journey cake," highlighting its convenience for travelers.
In different U.S. regions the bread is known by various names: "hoecake," "corn cake," or "syrup cake."
Traditionally it was served with maple syrup, butter, or fried bacon.
Some recipes add milk, eggs or leavening agents for a softer crumb.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Cornmeal provides slow‑releasing energy, helping to keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Corn contains dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Gluten‑free (when made with pure cornmeal)
items.content: Johnnycake can be a safe option for people with celiac disease if prepared with gluten‑free cornmeal.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Cornmeal supplies thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The classic recipe contains no added oil, making it a relatively low‑calorie food.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cornmeal can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume johnnycake in moderation.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: Compared with many grains, cornmeal is low in protein, so the dish may need additional protein sources for a balanced meal.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot johnnycake spread with butter, maple syrup, honey or jam. It can also be cut into cubes for sandwiches, added to salads, or served alongside fried meats.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked johnnycake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven or skillet before serving.
